author.name: Nathaniel Pavel
credits: Zac-Kyoti: Sidechain Compressor's key tap and bus layout, which the Modwerk base's key bus that this module reads is made of

presentation.label: RINGMOD SC
presentation.summary: Ring mod sidechain: another track's level ducks this one, or its waveform ring-modulates, steps, rectifies or tremolos it.
presentation.overview: Put it on the track to be ducked and choose the KEY track. In DUCK the gain follows the key's peak, holding through the kick's zero crossings and recovering as it decays; in RING the key multiplies the audio, and S&H, RECT and SLEW shape that carrier. The key comes from the Modwerk base's key bus over USB, so it needs no other module and runs beside Sidechain Compressor.
highlights: DUCK: gain = 1 - DPTH x follow(peak of |key| over 13-26 ms): no buzz at the kick's zero crossings
A fixed 4x key boost brings a full-scale key track at the default AMP VOL to full (measured under the emulator)
RING: a ring modulator whose carrier is any of T1-T8
RING's S&H steps the carrier, RECT rectifies it (frequency doubled), SLEW turns it into the key's level (tremolo)
KEY is the first knob of the main page, so it can be locked and modulated
Reads the base's key bus (USB): no tap of its own, so it runs beside Sidechain Compressor
DPTH 0, KEY OFF or no key bus returns the input bit for bit
usage: Select RINGMOD SC on FX1 or FX2 of the track to duck and turn KEY (encoder A) to the kick's track; DPTH sets how deep.
Raise REL for a slower recovery and ATK to soften the onset; turn KLPF to about 30-50 so only the kick's body drives the duck.

MODE on the SETUP page switches to RING, where the key track multiplies the audio: turn S&H and RECT to 0 for the plain ring modulator, then raise S&H for steps, RECT for a rectified, frequency-doubled carrier and SLEW for a tremolo that follows the key.

controls.name: KEY
controls.doc: The track whose audio drives the gain; OFF = untouched.

controls.name: DPTH
controls.doc: How far the key moves the gain; 0 = untouched, 127 = full.

controls.name: KLPF
controls.doc: Low-pass on the key: 14 Hz at 0, an octave every 14 steps (about 100 Hz at 40), open at 127.

controls.name: ATK
controls.doc: DUCK: how slowly the gain falls; 0 is at once, then about 0.7 ms at 1 to 1.3 s at 127, doubling every 11.6 steps. RING (SLEW): 0 rings with the key itself; above 0 the key's level, smoothed over the same times, drives the gain (a tremolo that follows the key).

controls.name: HOLD
controls.doc: DUCK: how long the duck holds after each peak of the key, one to two windows of 32 + 16v samples (13 ms at 34, 0.7 ms at 0, 47 ms at 127). RING (S&H): a new key every 16v samples, held between (0 every sample, 0.36 ms at 1, 12 ms at 34, 46 ms at 127).

controls.name: REL
controls.doc: DUCK: how slowly the gain recovers once the key's peak drops, on ATK's scale (45 about 9 ms, 64 about 31 ms, 96 about 210 ms). RING (RECT): blends the key toward its rectified |key|; 0 is the key, 127 fully rectified (frequency doubled, never negative: an AM-like modulation).

controls.name: MODE
controls.doc: DUCK: the key's level pulls the gain down. RING: the key multiplies the audio. ATK, HOLD and REL read SLEW, S&H and RECT in RING.

limitations: Needs the Modwerk base's key bus, which only the USB base has (loader ABI 9, `requires keybus`), so it is USB-only: the configurator refuses card firmware with it (the site's rule for a package that requires a base feature). A card image built with it anyway has no key bus, and there the effect keeps its depth at 0 and passes the audio untouched.

While a Part in the bank uses RINGMOD SC the base's tap copies every track's audio on every block, on both cores, and its price counts toward RINGMOD SC: 51 chip cycles a sample a core, timed on an MKII (charged at 72 before). Installed but used in no Part of the bank, it costs nothing.
The key is taken before the key track's own effects.

The key is exact when its track is dispatched before this one on the same DSP core (T1-T4, T5-T8), 16 samples late when after, and 32 samples late across the cores (the key bus's latency, measured on an MKII for Sidechain Compressor; not yet with this module).
A MODE or KEY change fades the effect out, clears the key's state and fades back in over about 1 ms, so a KEY parameter lock shorter than that is not heard.
Installing or reinstalling Sidechain Compressor while RINGMOD SC is live re-zeroes the key bus once: up to about a block of silent key (by design of the base, not measured with this module).

On a base from before the module select step fix (on main's beta base since 22 October 2026), KEY may move one track per detent on the first visit to the main page after choosing the effect, until the page is entered again. With the fix, on the MKII development twin on 22 October 2026, it stepped cleanly from the first visit.

Declared conflict with Analog BD: carried over from the card builder's rule (Analog BD admits only the effects on its companion list, and this one is not on it). Over USB no resource clash is known; it is declared for every build until the owner decides otherwise, so the configurator never offers both.

DUCK buzzes at its very shortest settings: with ATK, HOLD and REL all near 0 the gain follows each cycle of the key, an audio-rate amplitude modulation (heard on an MKII with 0.1.0, as expected). Keep HOLD above half a cycle of the key for a clean duck.

A slow SLEW stops a little short of the key's level (each sample's rise is truncated to the word; up to about 1.4% of full scale at 127, as the review measured on the build before) and a very quiet key never raises it from 0; an LFO on S&H turns S&H 0 into a hold of 1 to 15 samples.

On an MKII (22 October 2026, over USB, a development twin of the beta base) DUCK, RING and its three knobs (SLEW turned through 0), two instances, Part and project reload and every install and removal order beside Sidechain Compressor were checked. Parameter locks and LFOs, scenes and the crossfader, eight instances a core and a power cycle are not tested on a unit.

storage.label: DSP program
storage.display: 351 words P per core, 22 words X per instance, no buffer
storage.conditions: Assembled with dsp_asm: 351 words, both payloads (one source). State is 22 words of the instance's existing r7 block. The key bus is the base's (Y $800-$9FF on each core and $202 words at the end of each core's half of the shared window); the package declares reads of them as its DSP claims and writes nothing outside its state. A 9-value KEY formatter, a MODE formatter with its renames and the shared wide dial are ColdFire data in its page recipe.

processing.label: DSP estimate
processing.conditions: tools/build/cycle_count.py: 63 cycles/sample in each mode loop (DUCK 63 as 0.1.0, RING 63 with S&H, RECT and SLEW). Measured with modules/ring-sc/perf.py (benchmark_stock_dsp.py's method, a private native image with the key bus's seed marks): at most 80.56 executed instructions/sample per instance with trig splits (67.69 unsplit), COMPRESSOR 72.06. The base's key bus tap, charged to the module while it is installed, adds 41 executed instructions a sample per core whatever is on the tracks (counted from its source, charged at 7/4). Not hardware cycles.

impact.conditions: One active instance at its dearest settings (DUCK; RING with every carrier stage on is cheaper). The base's key bus tap is a per-core cost while the module is installed. Emulator and static figures; no hardware timing.

cpu.rationale: A page recipe (two label formatters and the RING renames); no ColdFire code of its own.

dsp.rationale: At most 80.56 executed instructions/sample per instance with trig splits in perf.py's bench (DUCK, 67.69 unsplit; RING 79.19 / 67.00), against 72.06 for stock COMPRESSOR and 314.19 for SPRING REV in the same host. The base's key bus tap adds 41 executed instructions a sample per core while the module is installed (counted from its source).

memory.rationale: 351 words of DSP program per core and 22 words of state in each instance's existing block; the key bus's memory is the base's.

tests.summary: The assembled module matches a reference model within 1.8e-07 of full scale in both modes (the key's low-pass, RECT and SLEW's level in exact integers), passes the input bit for bit when the key bus is not live, and equals 0.1.0 sample for sample in DUCK and in RING with S&H, RECT and SLEW at 0; SLEW crosses 0 without a click and S&H turned down cuts its hold short. On 22 October 2026 its USB package 2ba32a49 ran on the author's MKII on a RAM-booted development twin of the beta base: DUCK, plain RING, RECT, SLEW through 0 and S&H by ear, two instances on both cores and slots, Part and project reload, every install and removal order beside Sidechain Compressor, and the base's self-test passed. Not run on a unit: parameter locks and LFOs, scenes, eight instances a core, a power cycle.
gates: verify.py: bit-exact passthrough (KEY OFF, DPTH 0, no key bus), DUCK and RING against the model over 576 settings, ATK, a steady and a decaying key, both key paths, trig splits, the mode fade, the memory guard, knob steps, and RING's carrier: S&H's hold, SLEW's level, RECT's rectification, SLEW across 0 once and every eight blocks without a click, S&H 127 to 0 taking a new key at once
compare02 (dsp_host) against 0.1.0: DUCK and RING with S&H, RECT and SLEW at 0 identical over 864 + 36 settings, the key paths, splits, mode switches and sweeps (TESTING.md)
tools/stress.py: eight instances with every knob moving for 30 s under dsp_host -guard -dirty
perf.py: bench against stock COMPRESSOR, SPRING REV, DARK REV and DJ EQ, and sixteen instances under -guard -guard-shared -dirty with LFOs, random slots and trig splits (evidence/performance.json)
tools/build/cycle_count.py: 63 cycles/sample in each mode loop
npm run module:verify -- ring-sc: the native comparison of every chooser selection (TESTING.md)

conditions.parameterExtremes: tools/build/cycle_count.py prices both straight-line mode loops at 63 cycles/sample with the key's bsr (DUCK as 0.1.0; RING with S&H, RECT, SLEW's crossfade and every ramp). perf.py bench ran the manifest's dearest settings in DUCK and RING with a trig split at every position, the defaults and the moving pattern: worst 80.56 executed instructions/sample (DUCK, split at 1), RING 79.19.
conditions.parameterModulation: The moving pattern changes every active slot every block; perf.py stress adds three LFOs a track (DPTH, KLPF, REL/RECT) and a new random value on every slot each sixteenth, KEY and MODE included. The render gate turns SLEW across 0 once and every eight blocks against the model. On the MKII SLEW was turned through 0 by hand; parameter locks and LFOs were not tried on a unit.
conditions.modeSwitching: A MODE or KEY change fades the depth to 0, adopts the change with the key's state cleared and ramps back (render gate 8); the stress run switches MODE and KEY every sixteenth under load, and the benchmark has a trig split at every position 1-15. MODE was switched by hand on the MKII, with Part and project reloads.
conditions.maxLoad: Eight instances a core (FX1 and FX2 of four tracks): 8 x 63 = 504, plus the base's key bus tap, charged at 72 a core while RINGMOD SC is installed: 576 of 3,120 usable static cycles a core. perf.py stress, sixteen instances for 32 s under -guard -guard-shared -dirty: no hang, no clobber, per-core peaks 638.1 and 636.8 executed instructions/sample. Two instances ran on the MKII (self-test passed); eight a core were not run on a unit.
conditions.inputConditions: Stress stems: drums with full-scale clicks, a full-level chord, noise bursts and silence, a sweep, a full-scale square, impulses and DC steps on the audio, eight different keys. Both mode loops are straight-line: no signal-dependent branch.

regions.name: Program: 351 P words on each DSP core (one source for both)
FX page recipe the base keeps (descriptor patches, KEY and MODE formatters, the RING renames)
State: 22 X words of the instance's existing r7 block

memory.conditions: From the USB package (2,416 bytes: 351 DSP words with four relocations, the 868-byte page recipe as sdk/runtime/loader/build.py lays it out, its claims and header) and the source's r7 block ($00-$15, zeroed by init). Sixteen instances are FX1 and FX2 of all eight tracks. No Y memory, no delay buffer, heap or ColdFire code of its own. The key bus's memory (Y $800-$9FF on each core and the last $202 words of each core's half of the shared window) is the base's, as are its tap and engine.

hardware.summary: Over USB on an Octatrack MKII, OS 1.40C, RAM-booted development twin 53ddaf60 of main's beta base with the module select step and key bus reader admission fixes (MAIN 712666cb..., never flashed); package 2ba32a49. By ear with a kick on T1 as KEY: DUCK, plain RING, RECT swept, SLEW through 0 turned quickly and slowly without a click, S&H 127 to 0 stopping at once; the names follow MODE; KEY steps cleanly on the first visit. Two instances (T4 FX1 DUCK, T5 FX2 RING) on both cores and slots, independent. Part SAVE/RELOAD and project save/load restore them with the bus live. Over USB: install alone and beside Sidechain Compressor share one bus; every removal order returns the bus and arena; removal in use refused (loader refusal 7). The base's self-test passed with Sidechain (CPU 52.8 %, T1-4 27.7 %, T5-8 37.5 %, longest frame 401 us) and with two instances (CPU 66.7 %, T1-4 21.8 %, T5-8 39.5 %, 384 us) (evidence/hardware.md).
limitations: Parameter locks and LFOs (a lock or LFO on SLEW through 0 included), scenes and the crossfader, the stale-seed install while playing, the window and buffer reads and the missing-module message were not run on a unit for any 0.2.0 build.
The key latency (T4 0, T2 16, T5 32 samples) is carried from the 21 October key bus re-check, not re-measured through this module.
A power cycle cannot be tested on a RAM-booted twin; not tested. The flashed main base was not used for this source.
The twin carries two base fixes that were still in review; eight instances a core and MKI were not run.
One MKII, one session, by the module's author; by ear, nothing on the unit recorded or measured.

tutorial.title: Quick tutorial
steps: Put a kick on T1 and a sustained bass on T2. Select T2, hold FUNC and press FX1, turn LEVEL to RINGMOD SC and press YES, then press FX1.
Turn encoder A until KEY reads T1. The bass dips with every kick and comes back as the kick decays; DPTH (encoder B) sets how deep.

Raise REL (encoder F) for a slower recovery, HOLD (encoder E) for a longer pump and ATK (encoder D) to soften the onset. Turn KLPF (encoder C) down to about 30-50 so only the kick's body drives the duck, not its click or other sounds on the key track.
Turn KEY back to OFF, or DPTH to 0, to hear the bass untouched.

For RING, hold FUNC and press FX1, set MODE to RING and press FX1 again. Turn S&H (encoder E) and RECT (encoder F) to 0: the bass is ring-modulated by the kick. Raise S&H for a stepped, sample-and-hold carrier, RECT for a rectified, frequency-doubled carrier, and SLEW (encoder D) to about 40-60 for a tremolo that follows the kick's level. Choose NONE in SETUP to remove the effect.

access.location: FUNC + FX1 or FUNC + FX2 SETUP on an audio track: the effect chooser (LEVEL selects, YES assigns).
steps: Put a kick on T1 and a sustained sound on T2, and select T2.
Hold FUNC and press FX1, turn LEVEL to RINGMOD SC and press YES, then press FX1 for the main page.
Turn encoder A until KEY reads T1; T2 dips with each kick.
For RING, hold FUNC and press FX1, set MODE to RING and press FX1: ATK, HOLD and REL read SLEW, S&H and RECT; turn S&H and RECT to 0 for the plain ring modulator.
Turn KEY back to OFF, or DPTH to 0, to hear the track untouched; choose NONE in SETUP to remove the effect.
